To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inactivated or attenuate SPPV vaccine can modulate the immune system in a local event at the site of injection and in a systemic event in the host.
SPPV is able to modulate the macrophage functions to its advantage, which provides clues to understand the interaction of the virus and host immune system.
the immunostimulatory effect of SPPV is a result of a local suppression of macrophage's functions that is followed by systemic stimulation of macrophage function and lymphocytes' response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the basic mechanisms of the immune response of sheep to SPPV.
the basic mechanisms of interaction of sheeppx virus with its host.
understanding the basic mechanisms that SPPV uses to modulate the immune response of its host.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the virus is capable of manipulating the macrophages' immune responses in a manner that benefits the virus and the host.
SPPV is a pathogen that has developed a sophisticated mechanism to escape from the host's immune system, and to protect its host from any fatal consequence of the immune system's suppression.
the immunostimulatory capacity of SPPV is a result of a balance between the immunosuppressive and immune-stimulatory mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SPPV is a virus that has evolved to survive in the immune system of its host.
the virus is able to modulate macrophage functions in a way that is beneficial to its own replication.
SPPV, in addition to its immunomodulating capacity, possesses an immunostimulating activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SPPV is able to modulate macrophage functions and the immune system of the host in a manner that allows it to survive and persist in the host.
the inactivated SPPVs can be used as a vaccine for other species.
the immunostimulatory capacity of inactivated SPPVs can be exploited in the development of new vaccines against different pathogens.
